'''Alastair Hugh Fitter''' {{post-nominals|GBR|CBE|FRS}} (born 20 June 1948) is a British [[ecologist]] at the [[University of York]].<ref>{{cite web| author=YESIUoY | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2dVp4ZflTc  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/h2dVp4ZflTc |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live| title=Alastair Fitter | website=[[YouTube]] | date=23 April 2013 | accessdate=5 May 2015 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Fitter was educated at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] and at [[University of Liverpool|Liverpool]], and came to the [[Department of Biology, University of York|Department of Biology in York]] in 1972.[https://www.york.ac.uk/biology/research/plant-biology/alastair-h-fitter/#profile] In 2004 he was appointed Pro-Vice-Chancellor, with the Research portfolio. He is a member of Council of the [[Natural Environment Research Council]].

Fitter's research interests include [[plant]] and microbial behaviour in a changing world; functional [[ecology]] of roots and mycorrhizal associations under field conditions; root system architecture; [[carbon cycling]] in [[soil]], especially in relation to mycorrhizas; phenological responses to climate change.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.york.ac.uk/biology/research/plant-biology/alastair-h-fitter/#research |title = Fitter, Professor Alastair H - Biology, University of York}}</ref>

Alastair Fitter is the son of the naturalist and author [[Richard Fitter]] (1913–2005), and together in 2002 they published an article in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''  on the changing [[phenology]] of wild flowers due to [[global warming]]. They have also collaborated on numerous field guides and other natural history books.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pure.york.ac.uk/portal/en/researchers/alastair-fitter(59eb31a2-e02a-4810-b894-b44b8e0b5a57)/publications.html|title=Prof. Alastair Fitter - Publications - Research Database, the University of York}}</ref>

Fitter was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2005.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.sebiology.org/publications/Bulletin/January06/Royal_soc.html | work=SEB Bulletin | date=January 2006 | title=The Royal Society welcomes two New Plant Scientists | accessdate=5 May 2015 }}</ref> He was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the 2010 New Year Honours for services to environmental science.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=59282 |date=31 December 2009 |page=7 |supp=y }}</ref>  He received a President's Medal from the [[British Ecological Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/membership-community/honours-awards-and-prizes/presidents-medal-2/|title = Winners of our President's Medal}}</ref> and in 2024 was awarded the Cadbury Medal from [[The Wildlife Trusts]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cdd60de9emeo|title = Naturalist who helped protect bog awarded medal}}</ref>
